text: To date, few human studies have endeavored to evaluate the effects of loaded stretch training on muscular development. Employing a within-subject design, Simpson and colleagues (81) had subjects perform 3 minutes of dorsiflexion of the nondominant leg on a leg press machine with a load equating to 20% of maximal voluntary contraction; loads were progressively increased by 5% weekly, with training carried out 5 days per week for 6 weeks. The authors reported significantly greater increases in gastrocnemius thickness in the stretched versus non-stretched limb.
